extends.description: The Acme Enterprise Extension builds on the core Acme Design System, adding enterprise-specific components, stricter accessibility requirements, and product-specific token overrides for the enterprise product suite.

items.title: Overview
items.body: The Enterprise Extension provides additional components, tokens, and guidelines required by Acme's enterprise product line — admin dashboards, data-heavy workflows, and compliance-sensitive interfaces. It inherits the full core system and layers enterprise-specific concerns on top.

items.description: When building an enterprise product within the Acme suite that requires data tables, advanced form patterns, or admin-specific UI.
When building a consumer-facing product that does not need enterprise-specific components or compliance constraints.

alternative.rationale: The core system provides everything needed for consumer products. The enterprise extension adds weight and complexity (additional tokens, stricter rules) that are unnecessary outside the enterprise product line.

items.guidance: Always install the core design system as a peer dependency alongside the enterprise extension. Do not use the extension without the core.
items.rationale: The extension inherits components, tokens, and guidelines from the core. Without the core installed, token references will be unresolved and inherited components will be missing.

items.guidance: When the enterprise extension provides an extended version of a core component (ex: enterprise Button), use the extension's version. Do not import both the core and extension versions of the same component.
items.rationale: Extended components are designed to be drop-in replacements. Importing both creates ambiguity about which version is in use and can cause style conflicts.

items.guidance: Enterprise products must meet WCAG 2.2 AA as a minimum. Components inherited from the core already meet this bar — do not weaken their accessibility behavior.
items.rationale: Enterprise customers include government agencies and regulated industries that contractually require AA compliance. Weakening inherited accessibility behavior (ex: removing aria attributes, reducing contrast) violates these contracts.

entityGroups.name: Enterprise Components
entityGroups.description: Components that extend or specialize core components for enterprise use cases, plus net-new enterprise-only components.

entities.name: Icon Button
entities.description: The enterprise Icon Button extends the core Icon Button with an additional 'tone' attribute for danger-styled destructive actions in admin interfaces, and stricter content guidelines. The core anatomy (a required accessible `label`, a slotted icon, no built-in sizing) is inherited without modification.

extends.description: Extends the core Icon Button with a 'tone' attribute for danger-styled admin actions and stricter content guidelines for enterprise compliance.

modifications.description: A 'tone' prop accepting 'default' or 'danger' that switches the button's token set to the enterprise danger palette. Used for destructive admin actions such as permanently deleting a record.
Added enterprise-specific content guidelines requiring the `label` attribute to use terminology from an approved list for compliance with enterprise UX writing standards.
Anatomy (slotted icon, required accessible label, no built-in size or color variants) inherited from core without changes.
All accessibility requirements inherited from core. The enterprise extension does not weaken any WCAG compliance behavior.

items.description: When the user needs to trigger an in-page action such as saving data or dismissing a panel, and no room exists for a visible text label.
When the action navigates to a different page or URL — use a link instead, which carries native navigation semantics.

items.name: Tone (extension-only)
items.description: Added by extension. No equivalent attribute exists on the core component.

values.name: Default
values.description: Added by extension. The standard icon-button appearance, matching the core component's default styling.

values.name: Danger
values.description: Added by extension. Uses the enterprise danger palette. Reserved for destructive admin actions.
values.rationale:
- Use when: The action permanently deletes or revokes something in an admin interface.
- Avoid when: Building consumer-facing UI, or for any non-destructive action. Use `default` instead — the danger tone exists to make irreversible actions visually distinct from routine ones.

properties.description: Switches the button's token set to the enterprise danger palette. When set to 'danger', the button uses enterprise-specific color tokens. This prop is additive — it does not change the core API surface.

items.guidance: Use terminology from the enterprise approved list for the `label` attribute on all icon buttons in admin interfaces.
items.rationale: Enterprise products are subject to UX writing reviews. Approved terminology ensures consistency across the admin suite and reduces review cycles.

items.guidance: Do not use the danger tone outside of destructive admin actions. Use the default tone for all other contexts.
items.rationale: The enterprise danger color is tied to irreversible actions. Using it elsewhere dilutes the signal and creates visual inconsistency.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Trigger a user-initiated in-page action using an icon, with no visible text label.

items.description: Use icon-button for icon-only, in-page actions; use a link for navigation to a URL.

items.guidance: Do not use for navigating to a different page or URL.
items.rationale: Buttons signal actions and links signal navigation. Assistive technology announces each differently, and users rely on that distinction to predict what a control will do.

items.guidance: Reserve the danger tone for irreversible actions.
items.rationale: When several tones compete for attention, the signal that an action is destructive gets lost.

items.guidance: Always set the `label` attribute.
items.rationale: Icon-only buttons without an accessible name are unusable with screen readers and fail WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

entities.name: Table
entities.description: The enterprise Table extends the core Table with a 'density' attribute for compact, data-heavy admin views, plus stricter guidance for large datasets. The core anatomy — a styled wrapper around a slotted native `<table>`, with a sticky header and responsive horizontal scroll on narrow viewports — is inherited without modification.

extends.description: Extends the core Table with a 'density' attribute for compact admin data views.

modifications.description: A 'density' prop accepting 'default' or 'compact' that tightens row padding for data-heavy admin views such as audit logs.
Added enterprise-specific guidance for datasets that regularly exceed a single viewport.
Anatomy (styled wrapper around a slotted native `<table>`) inherited from core without changes.
All accessibility requirements inherited from core. The enterprise extension does not weaken any WCAG compliance behavior.

items.description: When displaying tabular admin data — audit logs, user lists, permission grids — inside a bounded, scrollable container.
When the content has fewer than a handful of rows and no real column structure.

alternative.rationale: A short, unstructured summary is often better served by a definition list or a callout than by a table wrapper.

items.name: Density (extension-only)
items.description: Added by extension. No equivalent attribute exists on the core component.

values.name: Default
values.description: Added by extension. Standard row padding, matching the core component's default styling.

values.name: Compact
values.description: Added by extension. Tightened row padding for dense, data-heavy admin views such as audit logs.

properties.description: Tightens row padding for data-heavy admin views. This prop is additive — it does not change the core API surface.

items.guidance: Always give the slotted table an accessible name via aria-label or a `<caption>` element.
items.rationale: Screen reader users need the table announced by name to understand what dataset they are navigating (WCAG 4.1.2).

items.guidance: Do not use the compact density for tables containing primary actions or long text content.
items.rationale: Tightened padding that works for short, scannable values (IDs, statuses, timestamps) crowds out interactive controls and wrapped text.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Display tabular admin records — audit logs, user lists, permission grids — inside a scrollable, bounded container.

items.description: Use table for structured tabular records; use a card or list pattern for content-first collections.

items.guidance: Always render inside a container with a bounded height.
items.rationale: The sticky header and horizontal-scroll fallback both depend on a bounded, scrollable container to have any effect.

items.guidance: Always give the table an accessible name via aria-label or an associated caption.
items.rationale: Screen reader users need the table announced by name to understand what dataset they are navigating (WCAG 4.1.2).

items.guidance: Do not use the table as a page-layout primitive.
items.rationale: It is a data component. Using it to arrange arbitrary UI couples layout to row/column semantics that assistive technology announces as data.

entityGroups.name: Enterprise Tokens
entityGroups.description: Tokens that extend or override core tokens for the enterprise product line.

children.description: The enterprise action color used for primary interactive elements in admin dashboards. Replaces the core primary blue (#0055b3) with enterprise teal (#00796b) to avoid conflict with informational blue indicators common in data-heavy admin UI.

metadata.summary: The enterprise primary action color — teal, replacing core blue for admin interfaces.

extends.description: The enterprise action color replaces the core primary blue with enterprise teal in admin interfaces. The core token's type, category, usage guidelines, and platform API mappings are inherited — only the resolved value changes.

modifications.description: Changed from '#0055b3' (core primary blue) to '#00796b' (enterprise teal).
All platform API mappings (CSS custom property, SCSS variable, JS constant, iOS/Android tokens) inherited from core.

items.description: When applying the primary action color to buttons, links, and interactive controls in enterprise admin interfaces.
When building consumer-facing Acme products.

alternative.rationale: Consumer products use the core primary blue. The enterprise teal is specific to the admin sub-brand.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Apply the enterprise action color to primary interactive elements in admin interfaces.

items.description: Use for primary interactive elements in admin surfaces; use color-action-primary in consumer products.
Use for action affordances only — never to color informational badges or status indicators. Keeping action teal distinct from informational blue is this token's reason to exist.

items.guidance: Text and icons on this background MUST meet WCAG AA — the token is contrast-qualified against white foregrounds only.
items.rationale: The teal value was audited with white text. Darker foregrounds can silently drop below the 4.5:1 threshold.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

metadata.summary: Hover state for the enterprise action color.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Apply the hover state of the enterprise action color.

items.description: Use only as the hover state of elements resting on color-action-enterprise; use the base token for resting states.

items.guidance: Apply on hover only. The pressed state uses color-action-enterprise-active.
items.rationale: Hover and pressed feedback must stay distinct so users can tell an armed control from an activated one.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

metadata.summary: Active/pressed state for the enterprise action color.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Apply the pressed (active) state of the enterprise action color.

items.description: Use only as the pressed state of elements resting on color-action-enterprise; use the base token for resting states.

items.guidance: Apply while the control is pressed only. The hover state uses color-action-enterprise-hover.
items.rationale: Hover and pressed feedback must stay distinct so users can tell an armed control from an activated one.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

metadata.summary: Background color for the enterprise button variant.

extends.description: Replaces the core primary button background with the enterprise teal action color.

modifications.description: Changed from core primary blue to enterprise teal.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Apply the background of the button's enterprise variant.

items.description: Use only inside the button component's enterprise variant; use color-action-enterprise for other admin action surfaces.

items.guidance: Pair with button-enterprise-text for the label and icon — the pair is contrast-qualified together.
items.rationale: Mixing this background with other text tokens breaks the audited contrast pairing.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

metadata.summary: Text color for the enterprise button variant.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Apply the label and icon color inside the button's enterprise variant.

items.description: Use only on the enterprise button backgrounds (resting, hover, and active); it is not a general-purpose text token.

items.guidance: Do not repurpose as an on-color text token for other components — it is qualified against the enterprise button backgrounds only.
items.rationale: Contrast was audited against the enterprise button background ramp, not against arbitrary filled surfaces.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

metadata.summary: Hover background for the enterprise button variant.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Apply the hover background of the button's enterprise variant.

items.description: Use only as the hover state of button-enterprise-bg; use the resting token everywhere else.

items.guidance: Apply on hover only. The pressed state uses button-enterprise-active-bg.
items.rationale: Hover and pressed feedback must stay distinct so users can tell an armed control from an activated one.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

metadata.summary: Active/pressed background for the enterprise button variant.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Apply the pressed (active) background of the button's enterprise variant.

items.description: Use only as the pressed state of button-enterprise-bg; use the resting token everywhere else.

items.guidance: Apply while the button is pressed only. The hover state uses button-enterprise-hover-bg.
items.rationale: Hover and pressed feedback must stay distinct so users can tell an armed control from an activated one.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

children.description: A subtle background color that distinguishes the header row from data rows. Enterprise-only token — no core equivalent.

metadata.summary: Background color for table column headers.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Distinguish the table's header row from its data rows.

items.description: Use only for the table header row; page-level and panel backgrounds use the core surface tokens.

items.guidance: Header text on this background MUST meet WCAG AA contrast.
items.rationale: Column headers carry sort affordances and labels — illegible headers make the whole grid unusable.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Give pointer-hover feedback on table rows.

items.description: Use for transient pointer feedback only; persistent selection uses color-table-row-selected.

items.guidance: Keep visually distinct from color-table-row-selected — users rely on the difference to tell hover from selection.
items.rationale: When hover and selected states look alike, users lose track of what is actually selected during bulk operations.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

items.description: Use for persistent selection only; transient pointer feedback uses color-table-row-hover.

items.guidance: Keep visually distinct from color-table-row-hover — users rely on the difference to tell selection from hover.
items.rationale: When hover and selected states look alike, users lose track of what is actually selected during bulk operations.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

children.description: Row block-padding used by the Table's enterprise-only 'compact' density. Enterprise-only token — no core equivalent, since the core Table exposes no density variant.

metadata.summary: Row padding for the table's compact density variant.

agentDocumentBlocks.purpose: Set row block-padding when the table's compact density is active.

items.description: Use only on the table's compact density; the default density uses the core row-padding token.

items.guidance: Do not apply outside of the compact density variant.
items.rationale: This value is tuned for short, scannable cell content only — applying it more broadly reintroduces the readability problems compact density is meant to avoid elsewhere.

items.guidance: Do not override this token value at the component level.
items.rationale: An override forks the value from its source of truth: palette updates stop propagating and contrast audits no longer see the real value.

items.title: Intent
items.body: The enterprise color layer over the core system: the teal action ramp (resting, hover, active) and component tokens for the enterprise icon button variant and the enterprise table.

items.guidance: Do not reference base palette tokens directly in component code.
items.rationale: Always reference semantic tokens that point to palette values.
